settings.reclassifyConfirm: Save the profile and re-classify all jobs (except APPLIED)? Takes 2-5 minutes and spends AI credit.

settings.anEngineIsAnAi: An engine is an AI subscription, an API key or a model on this computer. settings.pasteANewOneTo: Paste a new one to replace it
settings.keySavedInDatabase: Saved in your database and used instead of {envVar} from .env.

settings.onThisMachineNoKey: on this machine · no key needed
settings.forgetThisAddress: Forget this address and use {envVar} from .env

settings.scoresEveryFetchedJobKeep: Scores every fetched job; keep it cheap.
settings.measured20260905On: Measured 2026-09-05 on this lane: Haiku 4.5 answers a quick check in 21–26 s but returned JSON that could not be parsed in 2 of 3 calls, and each costs a retry. Sonnet 5 answered in 19 s with none — it is the default when this slot is empty.
settings.tasksHint: A task you untick goes to the next engine in the list that takes it, and this one is not its fallback either.
settings.tasksNoWebCheck: The web check is not offered here: this engine cannot search the web.
settings.aCeilingOnWhatThe: A ceiling on what the pay-per-token engines may bill in a month, with a warning before you reach it.
settings.budgetForBilledCallsUsd: Budget for billed calls, USD a month
settings.emptyNoBudgetAPlan: Empty = no budget. A plan or a local model never counts against it.
settings.aWarningOnYourAlert: A warning on your alert chats at 80 % and at 100 % of it, once each a month (UTC). Nothing is ever stopped: a missed match costs more than a cent.
settings.whichModelDidWhatHow: Which model did what, how long it took and what it cost: AI usage
settings.whatEachFetchedJobCosts: What each fetched job costs before it reaches you.
settings.everyJobGoesStraightTo: Every job goes straight to the full classifier. Highest precision, full cost.
settings.aShortYesNoPrefilter: A short yes/no prefilter gates the full classifier. When most fetched jobs are off-target, spend drops ~30-40% with marginal precision loss.
settings.telegramChatsAndDiscordWebhooks: Telegram chats and Discord webhooks that receive job alerts.
settings.offSendsNothingToAny: Off sends nothing to any target; what is found meanwhile waits, and arrives in one message per chat when you switch it back on.
settings.aBoardUsuallyGoesQuiet: A board usually goes quiet because its slug was rotated. The quiet-sources card on Companies shows it whether this is on or off.
settings.oneLineInTheDaily: One line in the daily digest when a tracked board stops answering.
settings.anAlertHasNowhereTo: An alert has nowhere to go until a target exists. Add a Telegram chat or a Discord webhook below.
settings.applypackSendsATestMessage: ApplyPack sends a test message before saving.
settings.inDiscordServerSettingsIntegrat: In Discord: Server settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy URL.
settings.applypackPostsATestMessage: ApplyPack posts a test message before saving. The URL is a secret: anyone holding it can post to the channel.
settings.switchAWholeSourceFamily: Switch a whole source family off; per-company toggles on Companies still apply.
settings.keepTheAggregatorsOnThey: Keep the aggregators on: they carry the companies you do not track, and turning them off usually means near-zero new jobs.
settings.extraSourcesAFreeAccount: Extra sources — a free account of your own
settings.twoWiderSourcesEachBehind: Two wider sources, each behind a free account you register with the vendor. Until its values are saved here, a source stays out of the app.
settings.whenItIsWorthIt: When it is worth it, and what the vendor asks
settings.readyAddItOnCompanies: Ready. Add it on Companies → "Sources for your searches", then switch the row on.
settings.onceBothValuesAreSaved: Once both values are saved, add it on Companies → "Sources for your searches".
settings.theOtherSideOfThe: The other side of the table: rank a folder of resumes against one position. Off by default, because it reads other people's data.
settings.aScreeningIsOnePosition: A screening is one position and its applicants: the posting is read into a rubric you edit, every resume is stripped of the person before a model reads it, one independent call per applicant marks the evidence with quotes, and the code computes the score.
settings.employerHint: Adds a Screening section to the menu. The table is an order to talk to people in; the decisions stay yours.
settings.employerHintOpen: Adds a Screening section to the menu. The table is an order to talk to people in; the decisions stay yours. <link>Open Screening →</link>
settings.employerHintHidden: Adds a Screening section to the menu. The table is an order to talk to people in; the decisions stay yours. Turning it off hides {n, plural, one {# stored screening} other {# stored screenings}}; the files stay until their retention date.
settings.applicantsFilesAndEveryVerdict: Applicants' files and every verdict are deleted with the screening on its date. A hiring round, not a talent pool.
settings.retentionHint: {min}–{max} days; each screening's page can extend its own date.
settings.theWeeklyCleanupDeletesWhat: The weekly cleanup deletes what has passed its date. Deleting a screening yourself removes the files at once.
settings.everyScreeningCallGoesTo: Every screening call goes to the first engine that takes Screening applicants, with its resume model.
settings.aCliOnAPersonal: A CLI on a personal subscription runs under terms and data settings the subscriber controls, not the employer. For applicants’ data the defensible path is an API engine under a data-processing agreement, or a local model through the OpenAI-compatible engine (a localhost base URL). The screening page warns about this too; it does not block.
settings.anApiOrALocal: An API or a local model is what other people’s data should go through — check the vendor’s data-processing terms, or keep the model on your own machine.
settings.changeWhoTakesScreening: Change who takes Screening applicants on the AI engine tab.
settings.notLegalAdviceTheFacts: Not legal advice — the facts to check with whoever gives you that.
settings.pasteItIntoThePosting: Paste it into the posting or the reply applicants get. It says what reads the application, that no decision is automatic, what the tool never sees, and how to ask for a human review — the duties GDPR art. 13–14 and the AI Act's transparency rule put on the employer.

settings.pack.more: Only postings found after you switch this on are prepared, and only ones published recently — the jobs already stored are never walked. screening.applicant.heldBody: After redaction the leak check still found {kinds}, so no model has read this applicant. The redacted text below is exactly what one would read.
screening.applicant.orDelete: Or tick it on the screening page and Delete.
screening.applicant.sameAs: Another document of <link>applicant №{n}</link> — same email, phone or near-identical text. Scored on its own; keep the version you want and tick the other for Delete.
screening.applicant.stale: This scorecard was written under an earlier rubric. The screening page's Score button reads the applicant again with the current one; until then the number below is about a different yardstick.
screening.applicant.injection: The resume carried text addressed to an AI reader. It was ignored and the resume judged on its merits; see "Consistency" below.
screening.applicant.standout: Stands out — what no criterion asked
screening.applicant.standoutOld: Scored before stand-out facts were read; Score again on the screening page to get them.
screening.applicant.standoutNone: Nothing beyond the criteria stood out in the text.
screening.applicant.standoutHint: Read, never scored: a technology beyond the rubric, a number, a talk, a language. Each line is in the text.
screening.applicant.roles: Roles as the text gives them
screening.applicant.career: Career, read off the dates: {line}. Employer count and tenure are facts to ask about, never points.
screening.applicant.noRoles: No roles with dates the text carries — years, sectors and company types were left out of the score.
screening.applicant.pointsHint: Points are the answers × your stars, over the criteria the text could answer ({stars, plural, one {# star} other {# stars}} counted). Confidence {band}: {answered} of {total} criteria answered{thin, select, yes {, and the text is short} other {}}.
screening.applicant.decisionHint: The tool never sets this: a bucket is a fact about the resume, a decision is yours.
screening.applicant.reasonPlaceholder: Why — a referral, a fact the resume does not carry…
screening.applicant.adjustHint: Moves this applicant in the table and travels into the export with its reason. The computed score stays visible beside it — your correction is a fact about the person, not a change to the rubric.
screening.applicant.unseen: What the model did not see
screening.applicant.leakNone: Leak check after redaction: nothing identifying left.
screening.applicant.leakFound: Leak check found: {leaks} — read the text below before trusting the mark.
screening.applicant.notScored: Not scored yet — press Score on the screening page.
screening.applicant.lettersHint: {n, plural, one {Came with the resume.} other {Came with the resume.}} For you to read — never scored, never sent to a model.
